card.alive_premise: One partner tries to throw away the evidence of everything that did not work. The other reveals they kept it because those failures show how the person they love was made.
card.moment_origin_detail: Generic relationship hypothesis about a partner preserving rejected applications, abandoned drafts, or failed-attempt artifacts; no Aachu/Zuv lived fact is claimed.
card.title: The Box of Almosts
card.concrete_moment: During a cupboard clear-out, one partner finds a battered box containing an early rejection, crossed-out draft, expired pass, and other failed versions. The owner reaches to discard them; the keeper lays them in chronological order beside the current work that finally exists.
card.universal_truth: Being witnessed in love is not only having someone celebrate who you became; it is having someone remember the unsuccessful versions that carried you there.
card.audience_mirror: People whose partner saw the rejected applications, abandoned projects, awkward beginnings, or repeated restarts behind the version everyone else now praises.
card.scroll_stop: A person empties an apparent box of rubbish while their partner catches one crumpled page before it reaches the bin.
card.emotional_contradiction: Keeping someone’s failures can look backward-facing, yet the archive proves that their struggle was seen and their becoming was never invisible.
scene_proof: Worn papers, badges, and drafts fall toward a discard pile during a cupboard clear-out.
The partner catches one crumpled artifact before it reaches the bin.
The artifacts are arranged by date, each visibly different and increasingly developed.
The latest completed work is placed beside the oldest failed version while both partners remain physically present with the evidence.
card.relationship_motion: One partner moves from erasing the embarrassing past to examining it; the other moves from silent keeper to active witness, then returns the choice of what to keep.
retention_ladder: Why is the partner rescuing rubbish from the bin?
The first artifact reveals a rejection, but not why it matters.
More dated attempts establish that the keeping was deliberate.
The chronological arrangement reveals visible growth.
The current work completes the turn: the box held the making, not the loss.
card.payoff: The achievement may belong to one person, but the history of becoming belongs partly to the person who stayed close enough to remember every almost.
card.dm_send_reason: A viewer can send it to the partner who remembers their rejected or unfinished versions with the meaning: you saw the part nobody applauded.
card.format_recommendation: Illustrated carousel built as a cupboard-clear-out scene with a delayed chronological reveal.
card.asot_turn: Make the romance live in the slightly absurd domestic fact that one person’s throwaway pile is the other person’s fiercely kept evidence, without turning either partner into a rescuer.
card.novelty_fingerprint: cupboard purge + saved failure artifacts + chronological arrangement + apparent cruelty reverses into witnessed becoming
risks: Could become a static paper-artifact carousel unless every beat shows handling, resistance, and changed body language.
The final motion must return ownership and consent to the person whose work it is.
A real artifact trail requires creator confirmation before Aachu/Zuv personalization.
